items.t: Boundaries: NONE apply as a single market — an agent-profile page has no geographic market of its own. items.t: The regulator behind the person the page profiles: in BC, real estate trading services are regulated by the BC Financial Services Authority (BCFSA), and BCFSA states a licensed professional must give consumers information about commissions and fees, must only work for either the buyer or the seller in a transaction, must inform consumers of the duties owed to clients and non-clients, and must inform unrepresented consumers of the risks of dealing with a professional representing another party.

Surrey plans (the Surrey ground the profile serves): OCP = Surrey 2050 Official Community Plan Bylaw No. 21900 (adopted June 15, 2026) — Bylaw No. 18020 is REPLACED and is never cited as current. Zoning: Surrey Zoning By-law No. 12000 — parcel zoning confirmed per parcel in COSMOS. White Rock ground follows White Rock's own bylaws, not Surrey's.

Secondary suites (Bylaw No. 12000): one suite per single family, semi-detached or duplex dwelling unit; not within a coach house or garden suite; habitable floor area may not exceed 40% of the principal dwelling unit; a suite is not a separate strata lot.
Streamside setbacks: Part 7A of Zoning Bylaw No. 12000 sets streamside setbacks by stream class — there is no single riparian figure for Surrey.

Strata block — applies in full to any strata lot on the served ground, including a bare-land strata lot (Sea Ridge Bays form): Form B diligence (SPA s. 59; within 7 days, maximum $35 + 25¢/page — fees, amounts owed, levies, CRF balance, insurance summary, rules, budget and depreciation report); depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since November 24, 2022 (short-term restrictions may still apply by bylaw); only 55+ age bylaws valid under SPA ss. 123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions; a "45+" listing line is NOT a valid BC age bylaw.

faq.q: What protections do I have when I hire a real estate professional in BC?
faq.a: BCFSA states a licensed professional must give consumers information about commissions and fees, inform them of the duties owed to clients and non-clients, inform unrepresented consumers of the risks of dealing with a professional representing another party, and work for only the buyer or the seller in a transaction.

faq.q: The page says Jared grew up on a farm — is that relevant to a condo purchase?
faq.a: Only as the page states it: the biography says he grew up on a farm in Langley and lives in Langley now, and the page's specialty sections cover farm and acreage properties alongside its condo and townhome examples (a Morgan Crossing townhome). It is biography, not evidence about any building — condo diligence still runs through the Form B for the specific unit.
